audit.qualification: Three rotated repetitions of the unchanged16-workload diagnostic pilot. All raw samples, unfavorable changes, result/mode checks, startup/total/RSS/GC evidence retained. Source290 is the applied original, source292 the LF-only corrected baseline, source295 the no-LF shortcut candidate; all three run the same original sixteen workloads. The broader line diagnostic retains its sixty unchanged display-column mismatches and no full-correctness claim is made. Emaxx allocation counters remain explicitly unavailable. These are not calibrated nine-round/three-sample measurements and cannot establish the locked3% acceptance criterion or universal correctness.

application_decision.status: reject source295; no measured benefit sufficient to retain its added branch
application_decision.reason: The whole-buffer no-LF shortcut passes selected correctness but has no demonstrated useful speed gain. Undo is 2.036% slower and bytecode calls 4.842% slower than the LF-only baseline in this diagnostic; its raw aggregate is 0.997711. Preserve all samples without a significance or causal claim. Leave this optional optimization unapplied and continue the already recorded native call-copy lead. The independently necessary LF separator correction remains eligible on its own evidence.

scope.qualification: Three rotated repetitions of every unchanged 16-workload pilot for applied original290, LF-only corrected baseline292 and no-LF shortcut295. Every sample, unfavorable case and startup/total/RSS/GC report remains. Builds, tests and profiles were separate from timing. Allocation counters remain unavailable. This diagnostic does not certify calibrated nine-round acceptance or the unchanged upper 95% ratio of at most 1.03 for every case.
